scenario.goalStatement: When a customer makes a large purchase that is eligible for EMI, get them to convert that transaction to EMI before the request expires.

versions.plannerKind: deterministic (no model call in this slice)

conversation.text: When a customer makes a large purchase that is eligible for EMI, get them to convert that transaction to EMI before the request expires.
Understood. I have a few questions before I design this, then I will show you the campaign and what I assumed.
Which programs should this campaign target?
Should customers enter on the authorisation event, or on a scheduled audience pull?
On the authorisation event — we want to reach them while the purchase is fresh.
The EMI request ends up Successful.
How many reminders are acceptable before we stop?
I don't know — whatever is within our messaging policy.
Any channel preference for the first message?

I have designed a 2-message campaign entering on an EMI-eligible transaction, with a 7-day window to see whether the EMI request resolves. Two things I had to assume because you did not have the information: the channel (I used SMS) and the message budget (I used your policy cap of 4). I cannot tell you this will improve conversion — there is no performance data for Meridian Bank (FICTIONAL), and the channel-ordering idea behind my choice is an untested hypothesis, not an established result.

campaignConfigurationBlockers: No tenant context was supplied. The platform must pass the tenant the user selected before the conversation started; the agent must not ask again or infer one.

issuer.reason: No tenant context was supplied, so there is nothing to map to DripCampaign.issuer. The application models no "tenant" field (zero occurrences in src/), so the tenant -> issuer mapping is a platform fact the platform must assert — the agent does not derive it. issuer is REQUIRED by the model and by the application's own submit gate (DripBuilder.tsx:269), so rather than emit an empty value that would look configured, the whole campaign configuration is blocked.

id.reference: Agent-namespaced temporary identifier, not a value the Drip Campaign system issued or persisted. The real campaign id is owned by the application and is minted when the campaign is actually created. There is no import path, so nothing here has been persisted anywhere.

description.reference: agent-written summary; states that fields may be unresolved

applyToAllPrograms.reference: Deliberate STARTING configuration for this prototype: all current and future programs are in scope. Expressed with the model's own applyToAllPrograms flag rather than a program list. Not evidence-backed, and not the application's own default — the application defaults this to false (DripBuilder.tsx:89). The user can review and change the program scope before the campaign goes live.

programs.reference: Empty as part of the same all-programs starting configuration: the model ignores `programs` when applyToAllPrograms is true (DripCampaign comment, graphTypes.ts), so no program list is fabricated. The user can narrow the scope to specific programs before the campaign goes live. Note: scenario.simulatedAnswers.which_programs names a fictional program and is not used.

root.reference: journey graph built by the planner through the application's own dcConfirmAddNode

controlPct.reference: The application's own default for a new campaign is 10 (DripBuilder.tsx:91 `useState(initial?.controlPct ?? 10)`). Required by the model, so it cannot be omitted. Deliberately NOT presented as a bank-backed recommendation: softPreferences.preferredControlGroupPct is INVENTED and holds the same number by coincidence. Whether 10 is right for this campaign is a quality question for a reviewer.

status.reference: DRAFT — the only honest status while no import path exists. Activation is not the agent's to decide.

startDate.reason: No campaign objective window, no preparation lead time, and no real event calendar. The prototype's eventsCalendar is tagged INVENTED and is not evidence. Dates are left for a person to set.

guardrails.reason: DNC and NPA are campaign-level user choices owned by the existing system (GuardrailsStep.tsx). Both default to true in the UI (DripBuilder.tsx:95-96), but a UI default is not a confirmed choice. Omitted so the application's own default applies instead of the agent asserting consent.

allowReEntry.reason: A campaign-level user choice. The UI defaults it to false (DripBuilder.tsx:92), but no user input or explicitly adopted default supports emitting it here. Omitted rather than hardcoded.

reEntryCooloffDuration.reason: Only meaningful when allowReEntry is true, which is itself unresolved. No cool-off is invented.

unverified.description: No Send is configured to fire inside the issuer's quiet-hours window
unverified.unverifiedReason: 2 of 2 Send(s) have no determinable send time, so compliance with the window 21:00–09:00 (issuer configuration; INVENTED in this prototype) cannot be established either way — not that it is satisfied. dcn2 "EMI conversion offer": relative timing — fires 0 hours after Entry, whose wall-clock time is set by when the trigger occurs, so the send time is not knowable from the graph; dcn8 "EMI conversion reminder": relative timing — fires 0 hours after Previous Step, whose wall-clock time is set by when the trigger occurs, so the send time is not knowable from the graph. Determining these would require resolving the trigger's wall-clock time, which is a runtime fact, not a design-time one.
